issues.legal_issue: At the appointment stage, disputes concerning performance of construction services and related fee entitlement are referable under the construction-service agreements’ arbitration clauses rather than the share-sale agreements’ clauses when no breach of the core share-sale obligations is alleged.
material_facts: The parties had separate, subsisting share-sale agreements and construction-management agreements, each containing an arbitration clause with different seats and procedures.

The construction-management agreements set out the services, completion process, and fee entitlement; the share-sale agreements required construction obligations to be performed under those service agreements.
The dispute concerned rejection of completion notices and the resulting fee entitlement and payment, not the completed transfers of shares or an alleged breach of the core share-sale obligations.
The parties did not dispute the existence of an arbitrable dispute or the arbitration clauses in the construction-management agreements.
issues.conclusion: The appointment applications were maintainable, and the disputes could be referred under the arbitration clauses in the construction-management agreements. The Court did not finally determine the merits or the tribunal’s jurisdiction to identify the true source of the dispute.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11(6), read with Section 11(6-A), of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the court conducts a limited prima facie review of the written arbitration agreement and whether an arbitrable case is made out. It may look beyond the bare existence of a clause to reject manifestly untenable claims, but should refer a matter where non-arbitrability is arguable or requires fuller consideration. The court must read related agreements harmoniously and identify which clause covers the dispute. Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation supports the limited review and preference for referral where the issue is not clear; Olympus Superstructure Pvt. Ltd. v. Meena Vijay Khetan was distinguished because its main-contract clause was broader than the related-contract clause, unlike the clauses here.

predicates.application_for_appointment_of_arbitrato: A party applied for appointment of an arbitrator to resolve a dispute between the parties.
predicates.written_arbitration_clause_in_service_ag: The parties had a written service agreement containing an arbitration clause.
predicates.dispute_concerns_service_performance_or_: The dispute concerned performance of the services or a fee entitlement arising from them.
predicates.no_core_share_sale_breach_alleged: Neither party alleged that the dispute arose from a breach of the core obligations to transfer or purchase shares.

issues.definition: When an appointment application concerns a dispute about services or their related fees, and no core share-sale breach is alleged, the dispute is referred under the service agreement’s arbitration clause.

issues.legal_issue: When disputes under two separate but financially connected agreements require a common fee calculation, the same sole arbitrator may be appointed for both proceedings while the decision whether to consolidate them is left to that arbitrator.
material_facts: The disputes arose under two separate construction-management agreements, and the respondents asserted that the breaches and underlying facts were distinct.
A related fee-computation agreement required financial components of both projects to be considered when calculating the fee.
Separate proceedings risked duplicated effort and conflicting awards, while the agreements remained separate and the parties had not agreed to consolidate them.
issues.conclusion: The Court appointed the same sole arbitrator for both proceedings and left to that arbitrator the decision whether to consolidate the disputes and how to conduct the proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Proceedings originating in separate agreements should not ordinarily be consolidated unless the parties have agreed otherwise. However, where a related agreement makes calculation of a fee depend on financial components from both matters, using the same arbitrator can avoid wasted resources and conflicting awards. The arbitrator may decide whether consolidation and a composite award are appropriate.

predicates.applications_concern_two_separate_arbitr: The applications sought arbitration of disputes arising under two separate agreements.
predicates.related_fee_calculation_depends_on_both_: A related arrangement made the fee calculation depend on financial components from both matters.
predicates.separate_proceedings_risk_conflicting_aw: Separate proceedings could waste resources or produce conflicting awards.

issues.definition: Where two separate arbitration proceedings share a fee calculation dependent on both matters and separate proceedings risk conflicting awards, the same sole arbitrator is appointed and decides whether to consolidate them.

issues.legal_issue: A referral under a service agreement does not prevent the arbitrator from determining that the real dispute arises under a related share-sale agreement and ending the referred proceedings while leaving the parties to pursue the remedy available under that agreement.
material_facts: The Court referred the disputes under the construction-management agreements but noted that the true source of the dispute might instead be the share-sale agreements.
Determining whether the service conditions had been fulfilled and the fee had become payable involved factual questions for the arbitrator.
issues.conclusion: If the arbitrator finds that the real dispute stems from the share-sale agreements, the arbitrator may wind up the proceedings, leaving the parties at liberty to seek redress under the dispute-resolution provisions of those agreements.
issues.legal_principle: The limited referral-stage review does not usurp the arbitral tribunal’s role in deciding issues that require factual assessment. The principle of competence-competence, reflected in Section 16 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and discussed in Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation, supports leaving such questions to the tribunal where they cannot be conclusively resolved at the referral stage.

predicates.dispute_referred_under_service_agreement: The court referred a dispute to arbitration under a service agreement’s arbitration clause.
predicates.arbitrator_finds_real_dispute_arises_und: The arbitrator determines that the real dispute arises under a related share-sale agreement.

issues.definition: If a referred dispute is found by the arbitrator to arise under a related share-sale agreement, the arbitrator may end the proceedings and leave the parties to pursue the dispute-resolution process applicable to that agreement.
